findings.evidence: Higher.lean:87 `theorem MemWkpLoc.contDiffOn_comp_succ (hp : 2 < p) {k : ℕ} ... (hu : MemWkpLoc p Ω (k + 1) u) (huc : ContinuousOn u Ω) (hW : IsOpen W) (hg : ContDiffOn ℝ (k + 1) g W) (huW : MapsTo u Ω W)` has the same hypotheses as the new theorem, restricted to `p > 2`.

findings.evidence: Higher.lean:115 `contDiff_comp_succ (hp : 2 < p) ... (hg : ContDiff ℝ (k + 1) g)` and :123 `contDiffOn_comp_graph_succ (hp : 2 < p) ...` match the new globally-`Cᵏ` and graph theorems with `2 < p` replacing `1 < p ∧ 2 < k*p`.
findings.fix: Remove them and switch callers (`CauchyRiemann/Weak/Bootstrap.lean:141-142`, `PreciseRepresentative/Higher.lean:109`) to the `_of_two_lt_mul` forms, or make them one-line corollaries of those forms.
findings.issue: `MemWkpLoc.contDiff_comp_succ` and `MemWkpLoc.contDiffOn_comp_graph_succ` (line 123) duplicate the new `contDiff_comp_of_two_lt_mul` and `contDiffOn_comp_graph_of_two_lt_mul` on the `p > 2` subrange.

summary: The new `kp > 2` composition theorem strictly contains the `p > 2` theorems on main, but the PR keeps their separate proof, so the special case is proved twice. Derive the `p > 2` family from the new theorem, or remove it and point its callers at the general one.
